newsitem.title: UK: Halifax to wait for budget before moving rates.
newsitem.headline: Halifax to wait for budget before moving rates.

text.p: The Halifax Building Society said on Wednesday that it would probably wait until the UK budget on November 26 before making any adjustment to its mortgage rate.
"We'll be looking at the situation over the next week or so," Halifax's David Gilchrist told BBC Radio in an interview. "But we'll probably wait till the budget before we make a move."
He was responding to the Bank of England's decision to raise official UK interest rates by a quarter point to six percent.

Halifax said in a statement it hoped "this small corrective move will avoid the need for bigger increases between now and the election".The building society is Britain's biggest mortgage lender and its current standard variable mortgage rate, unchanged after the BoE's rate increase, is 6.99 percent. This was introduced for existing borrowers on August 1.
Halifax plans to shed its mutual status and convert to a publicly quoted bank in June next year.
